title: POC scoping - workload modeling - Veritas Finance
next_steps: Taylor to send annotated workload spreadsheet and sample logs by 2026-09-12
Jordan to share benchmark plan and scripts by 2026-09-14
Schedule security deep-dive with Veritas infra and security teams (proposed 2026-09-17)
Provide pricing estimate for 2-week dedicated pilot and burst capacity options by 2026-09-15
action_items: Taylor Kim: send annotated workload spreadsheet + sample traffic CSV - due 2026-09-12
Jordan Lee: propose benchmark config (models, batch sizes, QPS targets) + scripts - due 2026-09-14
Samir Patel: provide 7 days of anonymized request logs and SLO targets - due 2026-09-13
summary: Discovery and POC scoping focused on workload characterization for a 2-week benchmark pilot. Discussed current traffic profile, QPS/concurrency targets, token distributions, latency SLOs, and success criteria. Agreed to share logs, run Redwood-hosted benchmarks versus their on-prem model, and confirm timeline for pilot and security review.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted vs private deployment
transcript:
00:00 Taylor Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, start with quick intros, maybe a little context on what you want out of a POC
00:18 Samir Patel: hey thanks taylor, we mainly want to validate latency under realistic load and make sure costs scale predictably. we process user support chat + automated reconciliation flows, mixed short prompts and long completion tasks
00:34 Lena Ortiz: our current infra is mostly on-prem k8s with some burst to cloud, we see big peaks at end of day, and want to know if dedicated capacity or private deploy is better
00:50 Jordan Lee: great, to scope the workload we usually ask for qps histogram, sample requests, and token distribution. can you share typical qps and peak concurrency?
01:05 Priya Rao: typical steady qps is around 8 qps, peak spikes to about 95 qps for 2-3 minutes during batch job windows, concurrent outstanding requests go up to ~70, but those are backfills
01:22 Taylor Kim: ok 8 steady, 95 peak, concurrency near 70. what's the input/output token distribution?
01:35 Michael Chen: most chat messages are short - input tokens 20-80, but our reconciliation completions are long, outputs average 350-600 tokens, sometimes up to 1k for detailed reports
01:52 Jordan Lee: that distribution matters a lot for throughput and KV cache efficiency. for long outputs we hit memory usage on the model side, and batching behaves differently
02:05 Samir Patel: we have a soft p99 latency target of 300 ms for chat paths, and 2-3s acceptable for long report generation but we want median to be low
02:20 Taylor Kim: understood. for the POC success criteria, do you want: 1) meet latency SLO for chat under steady qps, 2) keep costs below X per 1000 tokens, 3) validate autoscaling and fallback behaviors?
02:34 Samir Patel: yes, and also demonstration of data isolation and audit logs for compliance, plus ability to pin models during the pilot
02:48 Jordan Lee: technically we'll recommend a benchmark matrix: run at 8 qps steady for 1 hour, run spike tests to 100 qps for 5 mins, run long completion throughput tests with 200-600 output tokens. target models: quantized 7B variant and a 13B fp16 or quantized 13B depending on memory.
03:12 Priya Rao: what's your typical hardware for the dedicated pool during benchmarks?
03:20 Jordan Lee: we usually use A100 80GB equivalent for dedicated pilot tests; for hosted we emulate with multi-tenant nodes. for private we can run on your on-prem GPUs if you want to provide access
03:34 Samir Patel: we'd prefer Redwood-managed dedicated for initial pilot, simpler for procurement. want to understand cost delta vs hosted though
03:42 Taylor Kim: we'll produce a cost model: baseline hosted per-token pricing, then dedicated reserved pricing for a small pool sized for your peak concurrency. also show impact of batching and KV cache; with prefix caching your chat costs drop significantly
03:58 Jordan Lee: curious about batching assumptions: given many short chats, continuous batching might increase latency if not tuned. we should test both 0-5 ms batching windows and aggressive batching to find sweet spot
04:18 Lena Ortiz: we can share production logs to help you model real inter-arrival times and tail behavior
04:25 Samir Patel: sending sample logs is an action item, we'll scrub PII and share this week
04:32 Taylor Kim: perfect. on benchmarks we'll want to run for a few configurations: single model baseline, quantized variants, and a smaller fallback model to evaluate graceful degradation. we'll capture p50/p90/p99 and tokens/sec and also per-token cost.
04:55 Jordan Lee: about concurrency math — with 70 concurrent and average response time 1s that's 70 rps if served serially, but model parallelism changes that. so we need to run realistic concurrency tests to capture queueing effects
05:15 Michael Chen: also interested in how session-state is handled, KV cache warmup times, and how that affects initial latency
05:28 Jordan Lee: KV cache warmup can add initial latency, but prefix caching and pre-warming common prompts reduces that. we can simulate session stickiness in the benchmark harness
05:40 Taylor Kim: security items: SSO/SAML integration, audit logs, KMS integration for keys, SOC2 controls, can we get your security questionnaire?
05:52 Samir Patel: yes we'll send the RFP security worksheet; we need network diagrams for private deployment and demo of audit logs
06:05 Jordan Lee: note — sometimes transcription says BPC instead of VPC in our notes, but we mean VPC wiring and private peering.
06:15 Priya Rao: small nit, how does Redwood charge for caching? is it per-token or flat?
06:22 Taylor Kim: caching reduces tokens served but billing is per output/input tokens; there are also fixed costs for dedicated pools. we'll show modeled monthly run rate under your traffic patterns in the cost workbook
06:35 Samir Patel: for the POC timeline, we want benchmarks done within 2 weeks of getting logs, and a follow-up to review results. is that feasible?
06:44 Jordan Lee: yes typical timeline: day 0-2 ingest logs & model workload, day 3-7 run initial benchmarks, day 8-10 iterate on tuning, day 11-14 finalize results and recommendations
06:55 Taylor Kim: would you want Redwood to run benchmarks in your cloud account for private parity tests, or run in our environment?
07:04 Lena Ortiz: prefer in our cloud to validate networking and egress, but we can also accept results from Redwood-hosted for initial pass
07:15 Jordan Lee: fine, for cloud tests we'll need a small service account and access to a test VPC; for Redwood-hosted we'll provide ephemeral dataset and configs
07:28 Samir Patel: competitors question: we've pilot-ed with OpenAI and saw predictable latency but cost was high; curious how you compare to Anthropic on reliability
07:40 Taylor Kim: we benchmark across models and show unit economics; for reliability our fallbacks and autoscaling policies help keep p99 bounded, we'll include comparative notes but won't claim vendor-specific numbers without tests
07:58 Jordan Lee: technical benchmarks we'll capture: QPS vs latency curve, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory headroom, and throughput for long-context runs (4k tokens) — note: our support for 4k context can be optimized differently per model
08:20 Priya Rao: can you simulate mixed traffic with both short chat and large report requests? that's essential
08:28 Jordan Lee: yes our harness supports mixed weighted workloads, you can provide the percentage mix in the spreadsheet
08:36 Taylor Kim: recap of success criteria: 1) meet chat p99 <= 300 ms for steady 8 qps; 2) handle 100 qps spike for 2-3 mins with graceful degradation and <1s retry fallback to smaller model; 3) provide cost estimate within 15% accuracy; 4) security signoff on audit logs and key management
09:02 Samir Patel: good summary, we'll review and confirm via email
09:10 Taylor Kim: last thing — we will also include an optional canary rollout plan and A/B test approach to compare model variants during the pilot
09:20 Michael Chen: ok thanks, looking forward to the workload spreadsheet, i'll pull legal and security into the next call
09:28 Taylor Kim: thanks all, we will follow up with docs and next steps, call ends
47:30 [call ended]
